background_notes.fact: For any metric space X, the extended distance obtained by viewing its finite distance in ℝ≥0∞ makes X an emetric space. Equipping X with the σ-algebra generated by its open sets makes it a Borel emetric space. These choices apply to Rn(n₀) and to MaxProd(Rn(n₀)); they impose no measurability condition on the subsets E or F.

background_notes.justification: Finite nonnegative distances embed in ℝ≥0∞ preserving zero, symmetry and the triangle inequality, so the metric yields an emetric. The σ-algebra generated by the open sets is the Borel structure by definition and can be chosen on each ambient space. The maximum distance satisfies the metric axioms: each component distance is bounded by its corresponding maximum, and max(a+c,b+d)≤max(a,b)+max(c,d) proves the triangle inequality from the two component inequalities. Both source signatures quantify over arbitrary subsets, so no subset measurability assumption is required.
